name: Bhagat Singh
title: Shaheed-e-Azam
biography: Bhagat Singh was a charismatic Indian revolutionary whose martyrdom inspired millions of youth across British India. Deeply influenced by the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919 and anarchist-socialist literature, he transformed the freedom movement by infusing ideological depth into armed resistance.
early_life: Born into a Sandhu Jat Sikh family involved in anti-colonial agitation, Bhagat Singh read extensively in European history, socialism, and philosophy at National College, Lahore.
historical_context: The 1920s witnessed growing disillusionment among youth following the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement. The British decision to form the all-White Simon Commission in 1928 led to widespread protests, during which veteran leader Lala Lajpat Rai was fatally beaten by police.
major_contributions: Founded the Naujawan Bharat Sabha in 1926 to unite youth across communal lines.
Avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai alongside Chandrashekhar Azad, Rajguru, and Sukhdev.
Threw non-lethal smoke bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly in 1929 to protest oppressive bills ('To make the deaf hear').
Conducted a historic 63-day hunger strike in Central Jail Lahore demanding equal rights for political prisoners.
quotes: They may kill me, but they cannot kill my ideas. They can crush my body, but they will not be able to crush my spirit.
Revolution is an inalienable right of mankind. Freedom is an imperishable birth right of all.

sources.title: National Archives of India - Records on Lahore Conspiracy Case
Selected Writings of Shaheed Bhagat Singh

name: Rani Lakshmibai
title: Jhansi Ki Rani
biography: Rani Lakshmibai was the Queen of the Maratha-ruled Jhansi principality and a pivotal leader of the Indian Rebellion of 1857. Refusing to surrender Jhansi under Lord Dalhousie's annexation doctrine (Doctrine of Lapse), she personally led troops into battle against British forces.
early_life: Named Manikarnika Tambe, she grew up learning martial arts, horse riding, and sword fighting alongside Nana Saheb and Tatya Tope in Bithoor.
historical_context: The aggressive British expansionism through the Doctrine of Lapse disenfranchised royal states across India, uniting monarchs, sepoys, and peasants in the 1857 War of Independence.
major_contributions: Defended the fort of Jhansi against General Hugh Rose's besieging army in 1858.
Escaped from Jhansi on horseback with her infant son Damodar Rao secured to her back.
Captured Gwalior Fort alongside Tatya Tope to rally anti-British forces across central India.
Fought courageously at Kotah-ki-Serai near Gwalior where she attained martyrdom in battle.
quotes: I will not yield my Jhansi! (Main apni Jhansi nahi doongi!)

name: Subhas Chandra Bose
title: Netaji
biography: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was an incandescent nationalist leader who established the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) and led the Indian National Army (INA) in armed conflict against British imperial forces during World War II.
early_life: Qualified for the elite Indian Civil Service (ICS) in England but resigned in 1921 stating that 'no single system can be built on the subordination of one nation to another'.
historical_context: Believing that Britain's difficulty during WWII was India's opportunity, Bose escaped British house arrest in Kolkata in 1941 in a daring journey across Kabul, Moscow, Berlin, and Singapore.
major_contributions: Elected President of the Indian National Congress in 1938 and 1939.
Founded the Forward Bloc within Congress to mobilize radical anti-colonial elements.
Proclaimed the Provisional Government of Azad Hind in Singapore in October 1943.
Led the INA's Imphal and Kohima campaigns, raising the tricolor on Indian soil in Moirang, Manipur.
quotes: Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!
It is only on the basis of undiluted patriotism, complete self-sacrifice and uncompromising honour that we can build a free India.

name: Alluri Sitarama Raju
title: Manyam Veerudu (Hero of the Jungles)
biography: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the historic Rampa Rebellion of 1922–1924 against the British Raj in the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh. He mobilized tribal (Adivasi) communities against the exploitative 1882 Madras Forest Act which restricted their traditional Podu cultivation.
early_life: Studied astrology, medicine, and traditional warfare in Visakhapatnam and East Godavari before dedicating his life to tribal welfare.
historical_context: The colonial forest laws turned native tribal communities into trespassers on their ancestral lands, triggering fierce guerrilla warfare in the hilly agency tracts.
major_contributions: Organized traditional Koya and Konda Dora tribes into an effective guerrilla fighting force.
Executed raid operations on police stations at Chintapalle, Rampa, and Addateegala to capture arms and ammunition.
Defeated British military detachments under Assam Rifles using knowledge of jungle terrain.
Martyred in May 1924 after surrendering to protect innocent villagers from military reprisals.
quotes: The forest belongs to the sons of the soil. No foreign power has the right to steal our ancestral home.

sources.title: Government of Andhra Pradesh Freedom Archives

name: Sarojini Naidu
title: Nightingale of India
biography: Sarojini Naidu was a celebrated poet, suffragist, and political leader. She became the first Indian woman to serve as President of the Indian National Congress (1925) and subsequently the first female Governor of an Indian state (United Provinces).
early_life: Educated at King's College London and Girton College Cambridge, she wrote exquisite poetry before answering Gopal Krishna Gokhale's call to join the freedom movement.
historical_context: Women played an indispensable role in Gandhian satyagraha movements, picketing liquor shops, making illegal salt, and leading mass demonstrations.
major_contributions: Led the legendary Dharasana Salt Satyagraha raid in May 1930 after Mahatma Gandhi's arrest.
Presided over the 1925 Kanpur session of the Indian National Congress.
Represented Indian women at the Second Round Table Conference in London in 1931.
Advocated for women's franchise and gender equality in independent India's Constitution drafting.
quotes: A country's greatness lies in its undying ideals of love and sacrifice that inspire the mothers of the race.
When there is oppression, the only honourable position for a self-respecting person is resistance.

sources.title: Gandhi Heritage Portal - Sarojini Naidu Papers

name: Birsa Munda
title: Dharti Aba (Father of the Earth)
biography: Birsa Munda was an iconic Adivasi freedom fighter and religious reformer who led the 'Ulgulan' (Great Tumult) movement against British agrarian encroachment and feudal land grab in Chhota Nagpur.
early_life: Deeply affected by Christian missionary activities and colonial landlord exploitation, he formulated the Birsait faith advocating Munda self-rule and indigenous identity.
historical_context: The British introduced the Zamindari system and British land laws into tribal belts, destroying traditional Khuntkatti (joint landholding) systems.
major_contributions: Rallied thousands of Munda tribespeople to revolt against British officers and zamindars between 1895 and 1900.
Demanded total restoration of tribal land rights and freedom from colonial taxes.
Fought British troops in the Dombari Hill battle using traditional bows and arrows.
Martyred at age 25 in Ranchi Jail, becoming a permanent symbol of indigenous sovereignty.
quotes: Let the kingdom of the Queen be ended and our kingdom be established! (Abua raj setar jana, maharani raj tundu jana!)

sources.title: National Archives of India - Chhota Nagpur Records

name: Mahatma Gandhi
title: Father of the Nation
biography: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi pioneered Ahimsa (non-violence) and Satyagraha (truth-force) as non-violent mass resistance tools, uniting millions across India and transforming the global anti-colonial movement.
early_life: Trained in law at Inner Temple London, developed satyagraha during 21 years of civil rights agitation against apartheid in South Africa before returning to India in 1915.
historical_context: Transformed the freedom struggle from an elite constitutional movement into a mass anti-imperialist crusade involving peasants, workers, women, and students.
major_contributions: Champaran (1917) and Kheda (1918) satyagrahas protecting indigo and cotton farmers.
Launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920 following the Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
Led the historic 240-mile Dandi Salt March in 1930 against the British salt monopoly.
Gave the call 'Do or Die' during the Quit India Movement in August 1942.
quotes: Be the change that you wish to see in the world.
In a gentle way, you can shake the world.
Freedom is not worth having if it does not include the freedom to make mistakes.

name: Aruna Asaf Ali
title: Heroine of 1942 Movement
biography: Aruna Asaf Ali was a fearless freedom fighter who rose to national prominence by hoisting the Indian National Congress flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai during the Quit India Movement in 1942, after all major leaders were arrested.
early_life: Educated at Sacred Heart Convent in Lahore and All Saints' College Nainital, she married nationalist leader Asaf Ali despite social opposition.
historical_context: On August 9, 1942, Operation Zero Hour saw the British arrest Gandhi and the entire Congress Working Committee overnight to crush Quit India. Aruna Asaf Ali stepped forward to lead underground resistance.
major_contributions: Hoisted the National Flag at Gowalia Tank Maidan on August 9, 1942, rallying millions.
Edited the underground nationalist monthly paper 'Inquilab' alongside Ram Manohar Lohia.
Evaded British arrest for 4 years while orchestrating underground resistance.
Posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1997.
quotes: No country can remain in bondage when its youth and women decide to break their chains.

sources.title: Quit India Movement Archives - Gowalia Tank Records
